title: Eval: Quality Monitoring Demo - Prompt Sets & Regression Alerts (Pearl Analytics)

Liam to share benchmark template and example prompt set CSV
Customer to grant limited eval access to 2 engineers for 2 weeks
action_items: Maya Chen - Send pricing and security docs - 2026-12-07

Anika Rao (Pearl) - Upload initial prompt set and baseline responses to Redwood console - 2026-12-10
summary: Demo of Redwood's Eval / Quality Monitoring features focused on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparisons. Showed Console workflow for creating prompt sets, running A/B evaluations, and configuring regression alerts tied to failure thresholds. Customer concerned about data residency, retention, and how benchmarks map to production traffic. Agreed to pilot with benchmark spreadsheet and 2-week eval access.
questions: How do regression alerts map to production routes?
Can we run large-scale A/B comparisons and get per-prompt deltas?
What data is retained and can it be redacted?
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-05 18:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Raj (Pearl - Head of ML), Sofia (Pearl - Data Platform), Ethan (Pearl - CTO), Anika (Pearl - ML Eng)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're gonna run through Redwood's eval and quality monitoring flow, mostly prompt sets, regression alerts and A slash B comparisons, hope that works.
[00:12] Raj: Yep that works, thanks Maya. Quick note, we're short on time so if we could focus on how this ties back to prod routes and cost, that'd be ideal.
[00:20] Liam: Totally, we'll hit the console path first then show API calls and the optimize sugges- suggestions for batching and quant profiles.
[00:30] Priya: Quick housekeeping: recording is on.
[00:34] Sofia: Cool thanks.
[00:40] Liam: Alright jumping into the console, so this is the "Eval" tab, we create a prompt set \u2014 think of it as a test suite \u2014 you can upload CSV or paste, each row is an example with metadata, labels, expected outputs, etc.
[00:55] Raj: Can we tie a prompt set to a particular model pin and route? In production we hit /v1/generate with a model alias.
[01:05] Liam: Yes you can pin a model version on the eval run, and we support associating it with a route so alerts get routed to the right owner; the alert will reference the route ID and model version.
[01:18] Anika: How about A/B? We do A/B at request level in prod using feature flags.
[01:24] Priya: For A slash B in evals we let you define two model variants or two prompt transforms, run them across the prompt set and compute per-example deltas and aggregated metrics \u2014 we show p-values and confidence intervals in the UI.
[01:38] Ethan: That's helpful. Is the math reproducible? Like can we export the raw diffs?
[01:42] Liam: Yep export CSV / JSON, raw responses, token-level costs and timing, per-example score breakdowns.
[01:50] Raj: Remind me how scoring works \u2014 do we do exact match, fuzzy, or custom metrics?
[01:56] Liam: We have built-in metrics: exact, token overlap, embedding-similarity (cosine) and you can plug in custom evaluators as a webhook or run a local script and upload scores.
[02:08] Anika: If we upload their expected answer, can we do multiple canonical answers? We have many equivalent phrasings.
[02:13] Priya: Yes you can list multiple accepted answers and weighting; or use embeddings to compute nearest canonical.
[02:20] [02:20] Sofia: Ok on security, what data is stored? We need to know retention and ability to redact.
[02:26] Maya: Great question. For hosted we retain eval artifacts for 90 days by default, can be changed for enterprise/private. All stored artifacts are encrypted at rest; we integrate with customer KMS for Private. We also have a redaction tool to drop PII before storing.
[02:42] Raj: Does that include input prompt text? We have HIPAA-ish constraints sometimes.
[02:46] Maya: You can configure to not persist inputs or to hash them; for Private deployments everything stays in your VPC and audit logs are customer owned.
[02:57] Liam: Demo time \u2014 I'm going to upload a sample CSV. This one has 120 rows, each row has id, input, expected, cohort tags.
[03:08] [03:08] Liam: Uploading... small glitch with the first row headers, so the UI auto-matched, sometimes the parser guesses wrong \u2014 small note.
[03:18] Anika: That happened to us in other tools too, not a blocker.
[03:21] Liam: Once uploaded you can preview a handful, map fields, set scoring rules per column. Then you run a baseline against your pinned model. Running now.
[03:34] [03:34] Liam: Run kicked off \u2014 estimated time 2m. While that runs, let's talk about regression alerts. You define an objective: metric, threshold, window and sensitivity.
[03:48] Maya: For example you might alert if median embedding-similarity drops by >3% vs baseline over 1k requests.
[03:57] Raj: What's the false positive rate like? Our ops team hates noisy alerts.
[04:02] Priya: We support tunable sensitivity, 3 sigma rules, and holdouts \u2014 you can require both statistical and business thresholds before firing. Also you can configure a cool-off period.
[04:15] Sofia: Can alerts feed into pagerduty / slack?
[04:18] Liam: Yes integrations for Slack, PagerDuty, webhooks. You can also use a JSON payload to attach samples and diffs.
[04:25] [04:25] Liam: Baseline finished. Summary: pass rate 87%, mean token cost 0.0034, median latency 120ms on our hosted infra.
[04:34] Raj: Ok so the numbers are synthetic \u2014 how do we map it to our prod distribution?
[04:38] Liam: We recommend running a traffic-sampling job \u2014 Redwood can replay anonymized requests from a sampling endpoint or you can upload a sample of prod traffic. Then we compute weighted metrics by cohort.
[04:51] Ethan: Do you support per-route overrides? We might have a high-priority route with stricter thresholds.
[04:56] Maya: Yes route-level policies are supported, and you can set different baselines per route.
[05:02] Anika: About A/B \u2014 does Redwood run statistical tests for significance? We need that for product signoff.
[05:08] Liam: We run t-tests, bootstrap CIs, and Bayesian alternatives; UI shows effect size and recommended sample size.
[05:16] Raj: If the candidate model is cheaper but slightly worse, can we do cost-adjusted metrics?
[05:21] Priya: Yes you can compose metrics \u2014 e.g. quality minus lambda times cost \u2014 and set that as your objective for alerts or automated rollouts.
[05:30] [05:30] Sofia: On the API side, can we trigger eval runs programmatically after CI merges?
[05:36] Liam: Absolutely. There's an eval-runs endpoint; you POST a prompt set ID plus model pins and we stream progress. We also support webhook callbacks and status polling.
[05:46] Anika: Do you have rate limits for eval runs? We might kick off large scale stuff.
[05:51] Liam: For hosted there are quotas; for Dedicated or Private you can run at scale \u2014 we can allocate batch queues. We'll include recommended batch sizing in the benchmark template.
[06:02] [06:02] Raj: A little nit \u2014 I saw "KV cash" mentioned in docs once, can you clarify?
[06:07] Liam: Heh yes that's a transcription-ish note: we mean "KV cache" \u2014 prefix caching for incremental generation, not cash.
[06:13] Maya: Back to security \u2014 what about SSO / SAML for access to the console and RBAC?
[06:19] Priya: We support SSO, SCIM, role-based access control; you can map groups to project roles. Audit logs are exportable.
[06:27] Ethan: For Private we need customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations and on-prem auditability.
[06:33] Maya: We support KMS and can sign agreements for bring-your-own-hardware in on-prem packages.
[06:40] [06:40] Liam: Showing the A/B results view \u2014 here's per-example diff heatmap, red means candidate underperforms, green means improves. Click into any example to see both responses and token-level timing and cost.
[06:55] Anika: Can we ask for anonymized logs to be removed automatically after X days?
[06:59] Maya: Yes retention policies are configurable per-project.
[07:03] Raj: Let's talk about running periodic regression checks. Can we schedule nightly or on deploy?
[07:09] Liam: Both \u2014 schedule or CI-trigger. Many customers run a nightly regression suite against canary traffic, then alert if regressions exceed thresholds.
[07:18] Sofia: Ok show me the integration with our issue tracker \u2014 we want a ticket with failing examples.
[07:23] Priya: You can create an issue from the UI; attachments include example diffs and a link to reproduce the prompt.
[07:31] [07:31] Liam: We're going to demo automated rollback: you can create a rollout policy that will revert traffic if quality drops by more than threshold for more than N minutes.
[07:42] Ethan: That sounds critical. How much time to rollback?
[07:45] Maya: Rollbacks are immediate at routing layer, typically within one request boundary; depends on your network and route config.
[07:52] Raj: Do we need a separate Dedicated pool for rollbacks?
[07:55] Priya: Not necessarily, you can fallback to a different model variant on the same infra; but for guaranteed capacity we recommend Dedicated for core routes.
[08:05] [08:05] Sofia: Let's say we run an A/B with model A and model B and B is faster but 1% lower on accuracy; can we get per-cohort recommendations?
[08:12] Liam: Yes cohort analysis will show differences by tag \u2014 mobile vs desktop, by intent, etc. You can set different objectives per cohort.
[08:21] Anika: In terms of cost, how do you report per-route token cost?
[08:25] Liam: The eval export includes per-request token counts and a cost formula; Console gives aggregate cost metrics and token breakdown by model and route.
[08:33] Raj: Any gotchas with quantized models? We sometimes see weird regressions when quantizing.
[08:38] Priya: Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles and flags cases where quality dropped > X% during quantization; you can restrict quantization for specific prompt sets.
[08:48] [08:48] Liam: Also note we support model variants \u2014 if a quantized variant underperforms, you can keep a float fallback for critical routes.
[08:56] Ethan: How much effort is it to onboard?
[08:59] Maya: Pilot usually 2 weeks: create prompt sets, run baseline, tune thresholds, and set up alert integration. After pilot we can expand to Dedicated or Private if needed.
[09:10] Raj: What's the support SLA during pilot?
[09:13] Maya: Standard business-hours support; SE availability for setup tasks; for enterprise there's 24/7 and dedicated CSMs.
[09:21] Anika: Quick question about eval reproducibility \u2014 if we have nondeterministic model outputs how do you compare?
[09:27] Priya: You can set seed where supported, but we provide distributional metrics (median, percentiles) and embed-based similarity to account for variance.
[09:36] [09:36] Liam: Showing the API call now \u2014 POST /v1/evals/runs with body example, you can stream progress via SSE.
[09:46] Raj: We'll want to integrate with CI and run evals on PR, can the webhook payload include failing examples?
[09:51] Liam: Yes we can include the top-N failing examples and a link to the full run.
[09:57] Sofia: On the privacy front, do you run any eval compute on customer's side for Private?
[10:02] Maya: For Private we deploy an eval worker inside the customer's VPC so all data and compute stay on prem.
[10:09] [10:09] Raj: Any references or case studies for retail or finance?
[10:12] Maya: Yes we have case studies; I'll send a short deck with examples of A/B workflows and regression alerts.
[10:18] Liam: Back to the demo \u2014 here's how to set an alert: pick metric, baseline run, threshold, sensitivity and destination.
[10:25] Anika: Can the alert include model fingerprint and reproducible seed?
[10:29] Priya: It includes model version, config, and the run ID; seeds are included when available.
[10:36] [10:36] Liam: Walkthrough of the A/B dashboard: ranking table, volcano plot of effect size vs significance.
[10:44] Raj: What's the recommended sample size for lexical tasks?
[10:47] Liam: Depends on variance, but UI suggests N and will compute power given effect size; common numbers are 1k examples.
[10:55] Ethan: If we want to run a large A/B over 50k examples, any cost expectations?
[11:00] Maya: We'll share a pricing sketch \u2014 batch evals are charged on per-token or per-eval run depending on contract; Dedicated has different economics.
[11:10] [11:10] Priya: Ok I'm going to show the webhook payload example \u2014 includes summary metrics and sample diffs.
[11:19] Sofia: Can we configure retention of sample diffs shorter than metrics?
[11:22] Maya: Yes metrics can be retained longer while diffs expire earlier if you want.
[11:29] Raj: For compliance, do you have SOC 2 or ISO?
[11:33] Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II and are going through ISO 27001; security pack will include certs and architecture diagrams.
[11:40] [11:40] Anika: One last thing \u2014 if we want to tie regressions to model rollouts can Redwood automate canary analysis?
[11:46] Liam: Yes the rollout engine can do canary analysis and auto-promote or rollback based on your configured objectives.
[11:54] Maya: Ok we're nearing time \u2014 quick recap and next steps.
[12:00] Raj: Sounds good.
[12:03] Maya: Recap: we'll provision eval access for 2 users, share benchmark template, pricing + security docs; customer to upload initial prompt set and run baseline.
[12:14] Anika: We'll try to upload a 1k-example set and give feedback.
[12:18] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and Slack.
[12:23] End of call
notes: Customer is interested in pilot focused on prompt set evals, A/B comparisons, and integration with CI; main blockers are data residency and alert noise. Agreed pilot timeline and owners.
